newsitem.title: UK: Greenpeace says BP action could bankrupt it.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace says BP action could bankrupt it.

text.p: The environmental group Greenpeace said on Tuesday that it could be bankrupted by a 1.4 million pound ($2.3 million) damages suit brought by British Petroleum over a protest on an oil rig in the north Atlantic last week.

It appealed to supporters around the world for funds to fight the claim lodged in a Scottish court by BP over Greenpeace's eight-day occupation of the Stena Dee floating oil platform some 100 miles off the coast of Scotland.
"This action could threaten our future. We are down to the bone and so this is extremely serious and I think BP is perfectly aware of it," said Greenpeace spokesman Gerry Doyle.
Greenpeace UK said its assets had already been frozen pending an interim hearing in the Scottish courts later on Tuesday.

Four Greenpeace campaigners were fined on Monday for clambering aboard the Stena Dee floating platform which was heading from Norway to the Foinaven field some 100 miles off the coast of Scotland just over a week ago.
The protest was aimed at halting oil exploration in the area but the protest ended on Sunday after police arrested the activists.

"BP made 1.5 billion pounds profit in the first six months of the year - it makes more in profit in 48 hours than Greenpeace receives in income in a year," Greenpeace deputy executive director Chris Rose said.
"It would rather close down Greenpeace than change direction and invest in solar power. Greenpeace appeals to the public for its support," Rose added.
BP has denied Greenpeace's claim that it was trying to "crush defence of the environment".
"We are simply trying to regain some of the money we have lost as a result of their action," a BP spokesman said.

Greenpeace had also been blocking an Atlantic Richfield Co rig off the Alaskan coast to keep it away from a field in the Arctic Beaufort Sea. But a U.S. federal judge on Friday ordered the activists to stay outside a moving safety buffer around the mobile rig.
The blockades, aimed at fighting global warming, are part of Greenpeace's most ambitious campaign yet against the oil industry.
The group wants oil producers to switch to renewable resources, arguing that burning even existing reserves of fossil fuels will cause irreversible climate change. ($ = 0.620 British Pounds)
